title: I made a roguelite about one quiet drink that turns into a three-bar street war
author: zer0proof
selftext:
You throw beer bottles automatically, fight your way into three bars, and steal their signature attacks. Meanwhile, cars run people over and UFOs occasionally abduct the people you’re fighting. Things tend to get out of hand.

It’s called Saint Bender, and I’m looking for feedback on the opening: **is it clear how to claim your first bar, and does the combat get fun quickly enough?**

**Make the street do some of the fighting.** Cars plow through crowds, burning hoods become hazards, manhole covers launch into the air, and UFO abductions can lead to alien crossfire.

[Play free in your browser](https://zeroproof.itch.io/saint-bender) — desktop or tablet. Give it a go and let me know what you think. How does it feel? Does it make sense? Are things naturally easy to understand such as what to do, where to go, how to navigate menus, etc?

This is a rough prototype. I already have the idea laid out for level 2 but I'm still working on bringing everything together and I eventually want to replace all the art before moving on.

The workflow I used was a mixture of Claude and Codex. For anything that needed design such as menus and navigation I used Opus 5.5 and iterated upon each design for specific device sizes. For iPhone specifically I have a TestFlight version that looks different which is connected to MCP Unity that I playtest via my iPad and iPhone.

When something was off, I selected and manipulated elements in the canvas area until it looked good.

With codex, I used it mostly for the level design, testing, and TestFlight submissions. For the level design I think I can temporarily 'get away' with it due to how the assets sort of compliment the comic-book flat 2D look and how ridiculous the game is. The game still lacks real polish. At first the level just started off as a single street with a guy throwing bottles but then over time it went to a multi-street and 3 bar level into what is now even larger than that with a tattoo shop, parking lot, side alleyway etc. The biggest thing about this game is I wanted users to experiment and find random stuff as there are a few easter eggs in the game. One of them involve pressing a specific key on the keyboard 🤔. Another one kinda stinks.

I did use both for coding, depending on what was needed.

Artwork is my biggest pain point at the moment as I am only using Codex's placeholders. I typically have a hard time getting the art and when I do buy assets from real artists, they sometimes don't fit the brand or vision of my game so if anyone has any tips let me know as what you see in-game is 'ok' but it's not final and I am not pleased with the actual art at the moment.

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/zer0proof could you please add details on how AI was used to make this? Rule 4 is there to make sure promotional posts contribute by getting into the process and actual development. There's a real risk of the sub being swamped by self-promotion with nothing to discuss otherwise. If you don't update, this post may be removed.

replies.author: zer0proof
replies.body: Ok I updated the post is that better?

comments.author: fisj
comments.body:
Focus on details about development. What worked, what didnt work. Pipelines you build to control the models. Basically posts are supposed to cover the development process and share that so we can learn from each other. Saying you used AI to dev doesn't really cut it. :)

Here's one, you say you used codex for level design - how exactly did you do that? Traditionally LD is pretty hard to get right with AI.

replies.author: zer0proof
replies.body: Thanks for actually responding and not automatically deleting the post lol. Can you verify if what I wrote is ok or do you want more in-depth?

replies.author: fisj
replies.body: Yep, thanks for putting in the extra effort.
